questions.stem: According to Boyle's law, if the volume of a gas is halved at constant temperature, the pressure will:
questions.explanation: Boyle's law states that at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume (pV = constant). If the volume is halved, the particles have less space and collide with the walls more frequently, so the pressure doubles.

questions.stem: A gas has a pressure of 100 kPa at 300 K. If the temperature is increased to 600 K at constant volume, what is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: At constant volume, pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature (P/T = constant). If the temperature doubles from 300 K to 600 K, the pressure also doubles from 100 kPa to 200 kPa.
